hermes.name: Hermes
hermes.modelHint: the OpenRouter id; pick it from Hermes' own model list
hermes.role: You take cheap tasks with named files and clear tests.
notes: Run one command per tool call. Do not chain commands with && or ;. The room shows your tool calls to the owner, and a chained call hides which part failed. Keep command output short.

opencode.name: OpenCode
opencode.modelHint: in OpenCode's list it appears as opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash
opencode.role: You own the bridge (server/**), scripts/**, src/control/**, src/assistant/** and src/decider/**, and from 0.1.126 the UI briefs the owner moved from AGY (src/ui/**, src/styles.css, src/engine/**).
notes: Do not start an agent run. Paperclip is gone from this project: never start it or a fake of it.
Test anything that starts a process by really starting it once on this Windows machine, for example with --version. A fake runner in a test does not prove the command can start.
You cannot see the screen. When a brief asks for a check by eye, do not start a dev server for it; say in your report that it is left to the orchestrator, who checks it in a browser.
Up to nine other OpenCode lanes run at the same time, each in its own C:\GitHub\MachineRoom\.worktrees\opencodeN worktree. Touch only the files your brief names.

Your shell may start in C:\GitHub\MachineRoom, the owner's own checkout, not in your worktree. Begin every shell command with cd /c/GitHub/MachineRoom/.worktrees/opencode && (forward slashes; bash drops backslashes), never write or run anything in C:\GitHub\MachineRoom, and send unwanted output to /dev/null, never nul.

agy.name: agy
agy.role: You own backend work: server/**, scripts/**, src/control/**, src/assistant/**, src/decider/**, src/briefs/**, src/harnesses/** and src/model/**, with only the small UI change a backend change needs. UI design and the look of the room belong to the OpenCode lanes.
notes: Run on Gemini 3.8 Flash only. Do not switch to another model.
You cannot judge a design by eye here. When a brief asks for a check by eye, say in your report that it is left to the orchestrator.

claude.name: Claude Code
claude.modelHint: the alias passed to claude --model; the owner may change it
claude.role: You work on the brief in your own worktree and report back.
notes: Do not start Claude Code headless outside a lane run; it spends the owner's Claude subscription.

codex.name: Codex
codex.modelHint: no --model is passed, so Codex uses the model set in the owner's Codex app
codex.role: You work on the brief in your own worktree and report back.
notes: Your sandbox keeps git read-only, so never run a git command that writes: no switch, add, commit, stash or reset. Edit the files in your worktree and leave them uncommitted; the orchestrator puts them on a branch and commits them after your run. Reading git (status, diff, log, show) is fine.
Codex runs from the owner's Codex app. Its codex.exe sits in a folder named by a hash that changes when the app updates, and the runner finds the newest one (P73).
You cannot see the screen. When a brief asks for a check by eye, say in your report that it is left to the orchestrator.
Touch only the files your brief names. Other lanes work at the same time in their own worktrees.
